name: Dulaglutide
summary: A once-weekly GLP-1 receptor agonist with a long half-life and a cardiovascular-benefit trial (REWIND), delivered by a single-use autoinjector pen.
mechanism: Activates the GLP-1 receptor; the molecule is fused to an IgG4 Fc fragment, extending its circulating half-life and allowing weekly dosing.
pharmacodynamics: Lowers A1c and weight; reduced major adverse cardiovascular events in type 2 diabetes with prior CV disease or risk factors (REWIND).

dosing.adult: 0.75 mg SC once weekly, may increase to 1.5 mg weekly; up to 4.5 mg weekly in type 2 diabetes

contraindications: Personal or family history of medullary thyroid carcinoma
safety.overdose: Severe nausea, vomiting; supportive care. Hypoglycemia unlikely alone

indications: Cardiovascular risk reduction in type 2 diabetes with established CV disease or risk factors
clinicalPearls: REWIND enrolled mostly primary-prevention patients, making the CV case relevant beyond secondary prevention.
Fixed-dose autoinjector removes titration complexity for patients who tolerate the starting dose.
good: Simple once-weekly regimen, CV benefit, weight loss, low injection burden.
bad: GI intolerance, pancreatitis history, or patients preferring daily flexibility.
